title: one-shot-rollback-flow-draft
content:
Context:
- Quick notes for a lightweight "one-shot rollback" feature: allow an app or operator to route a single request (or single session interaction) to a previous model variant or fallback without changing global routing rules.
- Motivation: reduce blast radius when a new model/quantization introduces regressions or bad responses; give product teams a fast mitigant that requires minimal infra changes.

Problem statement:
- Today, rollbacks are coarse (traffic shift, canary adjustments) and slow to iterate for single-session failures.
- Users need the ability to immediately retry a single request with a different model or quality tier when an output is clearly wrong or expensive.

Goals:
- Provide a request-level API and simple console UX to trigger a one-shot rollback retry to a pinned fallback model/variant.
- Ensure minimal latency and secure audit trail for each rollback decision.
- Keep integration surface small for SDKs and hosted API.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full rollout/Canary tooling.
- Not intended for automated detection+rollback at large scale (that is a separate automation project).

User stories (rough):
- As an engineer, when I see a bad response in logs, I want to re-run that single request against the previous model variant and compare outputs, so I can determine if we should revert the rollout.
- As a customer support rep, I want to trigger a one-shot rollback for a customer session to quickly recover from a hallucination without affecting other customers.
- As a platform operator, I want the rollback request annotated and auditable so we can track frequency and trigger incident reviews.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- API: POST /v1/resend with fields {request_id, target_model_variant, sticky: optional boolean} returns a new response generated by the chosen variant and tags the new response with rollback_metadata.
- SDK: single-line helper in server SDKs to trigger retry with programmatic controls.
- Console: a clickable action in request trace detail to "Retry with fallback" for hosted customers (permissions controlled).
- Audit: every rollback attempt is logged with user, time, original_response_id, chosen_variant, and outcome (succeeds/fails).

Design sketches (implementation-level thoughts):
- Routing: implement an override header x-rw-rollback: <variant-id> that the router respects with highest precedence for that request.
- Stickiness: optional sticky flag to bind subsequent requests in the same session for N requests/minutes. Default = single request only.
- Security: only allowed for roles with rollback permission; header validated at the control plane (not just edge) to avoid unauthorized overrides.
- Latency: the override should not introduce extra proxy hops; router should map variant-id to existing serving pool.

Metrics and monitoring:
- Rollbacks per day (global + per-customer)
- Success delta: comparison of key metrics (toxicity score, exact-match, latency, token cost) before/after rollback
- Rollback latency (end-to-end)
- Top reasons (manual tag) in incident reviews
- Alert if rollback rate for a rollout crosses threshold (e.g., >0.5% of requests triggered rollback in 1hr)

Experiment plan:
- Phase 0 (internal): expose header override + SDK helper to internal teams only. Collect basic metrics, instrument traces, simple console button disabled for external users.
- Phase 1 (beta customers): expose console action with role gating to selected customers; run with default non-sticky behavior.
- Phase 2 (public): full rollout with tenant-level quota on rollback requests to prevent abuse.

Edge cases and constraints:
- Cost: repeated retries can double token usage; need quota and rate-limit per tenant/user. Consider cost credits for debugging.
- Consistency: if rollback changes tokenizer/quantization, outputs may not be comparable; communicate this in UX.
- Privacy: rollback may cause re-processing of PII — must follow retention/KMS rules and be logged appropriately.

Open questions (TODO):
- Should rollbacks accept "prompt modifications" (small instruction tweaks) as part of retry, or strictly only model variant? (Pros/cons list below).
- How to present diff between original and rollback outputs in the console? Simple side-by-side vs. semantic scoring overlay.
- Rollback quotas: per-user vs per-tenant; soft vs hard limits.
- Can we integrate a simple heuristic to recommend a rollback candidate variant automatically? (cost model + historical regression detection)

Implementation tasks (first pass):
- [ ] RFC for header semantics and security model (owner: platform eng)
- [ ] Add override handling in routing layer; map header -> variant pool (owner: serving-runtime)
- [ ] SDK helper + server-side example (owner: devex)
- [ ] Minimal console action UI for trace view (owner: console)
- [ ] Audit log schema + storage (owner: infra)
- [ ] Quota enforcement + billing considerations (owner: billing)

Notes / rough ideas: 
- "One-shot" can be extended to "n-shot" with a small TTL (e.g., 3 subsequent requests) if teams find single retry insufficient. Keep default = 1 to limit scope.
- For support flows, add optional "include_original_in_reply" flag so the support rep can see both outputs in the same chat bubble.
- Consider a low-friction keyboard shortcut in the debug console to trigger rollback for faster ops during incidents.

Quick UX copy (console):
- Button: Retry with fallback
- Modal: Choose fallback model (suggested: previous stable variant) | Sticky for next N requests? [checkbox] | Add note for audit (optional)

Example request sketch (for engineers):
- Original response id: resp_abc123
- POST /v1/resend body: {"original_response_id": "resp_abc123", "variant": "open-llama-13b-q4_prev", "sticky": false}
- Response: {"new_response_id": "resp_xyz789", "rollback_metadata": {"triggered_by": "ishaan@redwood", "variant": "open-llama-13b-q4_prev"}, "output": "..."}

Risks and mitigations:
- Abuse: rollbacks could be used to bypass content filters by re-sending with different safety settings. Mitigate by inheriting safety policy from original request and preventing downgrade.
- Cost spikes: add per-session and per-tenant budget enforcement; surface cost in console when retrying long responses.

Next steps:
1) Share with platform & devex for feedback (this doc)
2) Draft RFC for header semantics and console UX
3) Prototype header + SDK helper in internal env for 2 weeks

If this lands well, follow-ups: rollback heuristics, automated rollback suggestions, integration with incident workflows and runbooks.

Random scratch items (notes to self):
- Talk to Mika about quantization artifacts when comparing rollbacks
- Check with legal / privacy about re-processing flagged user data
- Add a small telemetry tag to the original request to tie the two attempts easily

-- end of draft (messy, please ignore formatting).
